so finally got my laser today

its a 20 mW hene with a powersupply

baught from meredith instrumes 

and it came with a nice little key.

so thats what i did:

i took the laser out of the box 

connected the male alden to the powersupply

wired the powersupplybox to my wallplug with a standard computer cable, 

was a good fit...

checked that the voltage was on 230 V for germany 

did exactly what was written in the instructions.

then i turned the key

nothing happened

the instruction says if everything is ok the indicator light on the powersupply should go on immediately 

didnt happen with mine

frightened i might have broke something i turned the key immidiately to the off position 

what did i do wrong ???

apart from the laser and the powersupply there was a small plug in the box sent by meredith.

its black about half an inch long and i could connect it to the powersupply next to the male alden connector 

what is that thing??? in the instructions it says something about a remote connector 

is that a vital part for running the laser ?????

please dont tell me i wrecked the whole thing already.

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md: Lasers typically have a jack on the power supply for connecting a remote switch for a door interlock. They usually need a jumper wire installed in the jack for the laser to work. Plug the jumper into its jack and try again!

posts.author: Tony
posts.content_md: CDRH regs require that lasers be marked with an absolute maximum output power rating, in your case 35mW. In fact, most lasers typically run around 1/2 of that number. It's amusing to see all the misinformation abounding on eBay because of this...

posts.author: frothychimp
posts.content_md:
Don't even get me going on eBay, lol. Ok, one peeve, and I know you've seen it: "This laser module is an OEM product for integration into a user end product and therefore is not required to comply with Title 21 CFR1040.10" If it lases when power is added it must conform to 1040 no ifs, ands, or buts unless it's homebuilt and sold as a working unit. Very few people are willing to sell working homebuilt units because of liability issues (plus there are FDA registration requirements for sales).

I'm a homebuilt laser enthusiast but I also sell commercial laser systems so nothing ruffles my feathers more than seeing that statement written next to a working commercial or lab laser system. Whenever I see that statement it tells me to watch out because the next statement about price and power will be too good to be true.

Ok, I'll get off the soapbox. I'm just a stickler for the law, lol. Regardless, I'm glad you got your HeNe working.

I look forward to trying out my own attempts at holograms as I've been interested in them for a long time but it always seemed like it was too much stuff to get set up and running (that and blasting holes in things never gets boring).
